Six from six in the league and back from Romania, the Lions host the one side that has come within two of them. Bristol sit second, have won four of their last five, and lost to London by two in September on a missed open jumper. [src:gs-standings] [src:club-report-bristol] [src:gs-bristol]

## Form: 6–0 in the SLB, 2–2 in Europe

Four games in ten days end on Saturday. The Lions beat Cheshire 87–83 on Sunday with a 10–0 run to close the first half and Joel Scott’s free throws with 13 seconds left, then held U-BT Cluj to 72 points on Wednesday after a 40–37 half-time lead. “Our defence, 72 points is crazy,” said head coach Tautvydas Sabonis. [src:club-report-cheshire] [src:club-report-cluj]

## Lions roster: and who to watch

### Thomas Kennedy

Leads the Lions in scoring on 60.9% from the field and has not taken a three. Went 7 of 7 inside at Cluj on Wednesday. [src:gs-lions-stats] [src:club-report-cluj]

### Joel Scott

Scored the late baskets and both closing free throws at Cheshire, then 15 points and five rebounds at Cluj. [src:club-report-cheshire] [src:club-report-cluj]

### Landrius Horton

Shoots 43.5% from three on 23 attempts. Led the Lions with 16 at Bristol in September, including the three that tied it late, and went 4 of 5 from deep at Cheshire. [src:gs-lions-stats] [src:club-report-bristol] [src:club-report-cheshire]

### Devante Jones

A 90% free-throw shooter who made both with 18.8 seconds left to beat Bristol in September. [src:gs-lions-stats] [src:club-report-bristol]

## The opposition: second, 4–2

Andreas Kapoulas’s side have won four of five in the league since losing to London, including 90–89 over Liverpool last Sunday when Davion Bailey’s left-handed lay-in with 16 seconds left stood up after two missed free throws at the other end. In between they went to Germany in the ENBL and lost 106–84 at Syntainics MBC. They have had six days off; the Lions have had three. [src:bf-recap] [src:bf-news] [src:gs-bristol]

They shoot threes, nearly 30 a game: Bailey takes more than seven, Zach Anderson more than six, and Diggins and Jennings nearly five each. Holden runs the offence and rebounds like a forward, but gives the ball away 3.3 times a game. [src:gs-bristol-stats]

### Davion Bailey

The Flyers’ scorer, taking 7.3 threes a game. Had 17 points, six assists and three steals against Liverpool last Sunday, and missed the open jumper that would have beaten London in September. [src:gs-bristol-stats] [src:bf-recap] [src:club-report-bristol]

### Michael Diggins Jr

The 2.07 m forward blocks two shots a game and takes nearly five threes. [src:gs-bristol-roster] [src:gs-bristol-stats]

### Cameron Holden

The point guard leads the team in rebounds and assists, and averages 3.3 turnovers. [src:gs-bristol-stats]

### Matteus Case

Scores his 10 points a game in 14 minutes off the bench, shooting 56.8% from the field. [src:gs-bristol-stats]

## Things to watch

- **Inside against outside.** Kennedy and Scott score almost entirely at the rim; Bristol take nearly 30 threes a game. Whichever shot falls decides it. [src:gs-lions-stats] [src:gs-bristol-stats]
- **Bristol’s turnovers.** Holden averages 3.3 and Jennings 2.2. Five Lions average more than a steal a game, and London took the ball off Cluj on an inbound on Wednesday. [src:gs-bristol-stats] [src:gs-lions-stats] [src:club-report-cluj]
- **The free-throw line.** September was decided there. Jones is 9 of 10 this season, Evans 18 of 21; Tarik Phillip is 5 of 14. [src:club-report-bristol] [src:gs-lions-stats]
- **Legs.** London played in Romania on Wednesday. Bristol last played on Sunday. [src:club-report-cluj] [src:bf-recap]

## Head to head: Lions by two in September

Bristol led 18–17 after a quarter, London by 14 in the second, tied at 47 in the third, and Holden’s free throws put the Flyers 78–75 up before Horton’s three and Jones’s two from the line. [src:club-report-bristol]
